page: Vultr vx1-g-2c-8g is a general-purpose virtual server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 1 physical AMD EPYC core with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is network-attached with a capacity of 1 GB, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. There are no GPUs bundled with this instance.

Performance benchmarks reveal a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance under stress-ng is highly competitive, ranking in the top tier (top 10%), which is mirrored by top-tier single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression speeds. However, multi-core performance is weak, falling into the bottom 25% for both stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core tests. Memory bandwidth is similarly constrained, with read-only bandwidth categorized as weak, though large-block write bandwidth remains average. Text processing is a relative strength, scoring in the top 25%.

Given the dedicated CPU allocation, the server offers stable execution for single-threaded tasks but suffers in highly parallelized workloads. Database performance is a notable bottleneck, with Passmark database operations scoring in the poor bottom 10% and Redis SET operations performing in the bottom 25%. Consequently, this server is poorly suited for heavy database hosting or complex multi-threaded applications. It is best utilized for lightweight general-purpose workloads, single-threaded processing tasks, static web serving, or basic text processing pipelines where single-core burst capabilities are beneficial but multi-core throughput is not critical.
